Our solutions range from tactical radios to radars, and from research to mission critical applications. About the role As a Senior RF Hardware Design Engineer, you will play a key role in the architecture, design, simulation, implementation, bring-up, and verification of RF and microwave hardware subsystems for aerospace and defence applications. The role includes RF signal-chain design from antenna port to baseband, including LNAs, PAs, mixers, filters, RF switches, attenuators, PLLs, frequency synthesizers, clock/LO distribution, and wideband RF front-end modules operating up to 40 GHz. The engineer will translate system-level requirements into circuit-level specifications and support the complete hardware development cycle from concept to qualification and production support. Key Responsibilities Circuit Design & Analysis Design and optimize RF/microwave circuits and subsystems, including LNAs, PAs, mixers, filters, RF switches, attenuators, VCOs, PLLs, frequency synthesizers, clock/LO distribution circuits, and RF front-end modules up to 40 GHz. Perform RF system and circuit-level analysis, including link budget, cascaded gain/noise figure, IP2/IP3, P1d B, dynamic range, SFDR, phase noise, jitter, LO leakage, image rejection, harmonic/spurious analysis, EVM, and emissions performance. Develop and execute RF simulation models using tools such as Keysight ADS, AWR Microwave Office, Ansys HFSS, CST Studio, or equivalent tools for linear, nonlinear, EM, and system-level co-simulation. Select and qualify active/passive RF components and design with Ga N/Ga As/Si Ge/CMOS RFIC/MMIC devices. Define component derating, worst-case analysis, lifecycle risk, alternate part strategy, and reliability considerations for high-reliability aerospace and defence hardware. Translate system-level requirements such as frequency range, sensitivity, output power, EVM, phase noise, isolation, spur level, and dynamic range into verifiable RF circuit and subsystem specifications. Systems Architecture & Integration Contribute to RF subsystem architecture trade studies and module-level implementation planning. Lead antenna-to-baseband RF signal-chain design for radar, EW, telemetry, tactical radio, SDR, wideband receiver, and up/down-converter applications. Work with system engineers to allocate RF performance budgets and cascade gain, noise figure, linearity, filtering, isolation, and dynamic range from antenna port to ADC/DAC interface. Define LO and clock architecture, including reference clock distribution, PLL/synthesizer selection, phase noise budgeting, spur management, synchronization, and frequency settling requirements. Guide and review RF PCB layout, including stack-up selection, controlled impedance routing, RF via transitions, grounding, return-current paths, shielding, cavity isolation, connector transitions, and mixed-signal partitioning. Support mechanical and thermal integration, including RF shielding, heat sinking, enclosure effects, RF cable/connector selection, vibration considerations, and high-power PA thermal design. Support integration with FPGA, firmware, embedded software, and DSP teams from the RF hardware side, including AGC, DPD, calibration, JESD204/LVDS interfaces, timing, synchronization, and hardware control interfaces. Product Development & Qualification Define and execute RF test plans covering conducted and radiated measurements, including S-parameters, gain, gain flatness, return loss, output power, P1d B, IP3, noise figure, phase noise, EVM, ACLR/ACPR, harmonic/spurious emissions, receiver sensitivity, blocking, isolation, and EMI/EMC pre-compliance. Perform prototype bring-up, lab debugging, tuning, rework support, failure analysis, oscillation/debug, spur hunting, desense investigation, thermal drift analysis, and simulation-to-measurement correlation. Support design readiness and qualification activities for MIL-STD-461 EMC and MIL-STD-810 environmental requirements. Support production transfer, including DFM/DFT review, BOM alternate qualification, test fixture definition, production test procedures, and yield/debug support. Maintain design documentation, including schematics, RF PCB specifications, simulation reports, test procedures, test reports, analysis reports, interface control documents, compliance matrices, and verification evidence. Prepare and present PDR/CDR material, technical status, risk items, and design trade-off summaries to program managers, internal teams, and external customers. Required Qualifications Tech / M.Tech. in Electrical and Electronics Engineering, or closely related field. 8+ years of hands-on RF/microwave circuit and subsystem design experience in an aerospace, defence environment Demonstrated proficiency with at least two RF EDA tools: Keysight ADS, AWR Microwave Office, Ansys HFSS, CST Studio, or equivalent. Strong command of RF test equipment: VNA, Spectrum Analyzer, signal generator, noise-figure Analyzer, Oscilloscope and power meters. Experience designing with Ga N/Ga As/Si Ge/CMOS RFIC/MMIC devices. Familiarity with MIL-STD-461, MIL-STD-810, and MIL-HDBK-217 requirements. Strong written and verbal communication skills; ability to produce and defend technical documentation in a program environment Preferred S. or Ph.D. in RF / Microwave Engineering or related discipline Experience with Radar, Electronic warfare (EW), or Telemetry systems Familiarity with VHDL/Verilog or Python/MATLAB for test automation and signal processing support. We work on leading technologies in Signal Processing solving problems in Defence and Aerospace fields. Our solutions range from tactical radios to radars, and from research to mission critical applications. About the role As a Senior RF Hardware Design Engineer, you will play a key role in the architecture, design, simulation, implementation, bring-up, and verification of RF and microwave hardware subsystems for aerospace and defence applications. The role includes RF signal-chain design from antenna port to baseband, including LNAs, PAs, mixers, filters, RF switches, attenuators, PLLs, frequency synthesizers, clock/LO distribution, and wideband RF front-end modules operating up to 40 GHz. The engineer will translate system-level requirements into circuit-level specifications and support the complete hardware development cycle from concept to qualification and production support. Key Responsibilities Circuit Design & Analysis Design and optimize RF/microwave circuits and subsystems, including LNAs, PAs, mixers, filters, RF switches, attenuators, VCOs, PLLs, frequency synthesizers, clock/LO distribution circuits, and RF front-end modules up to 40 GHz. Perform RF system and circuit-level analysis, including link budget, cascaded gain/noise figure, IP2/IP3, P1d B, dynamic range, SFDR, phase noise, jitter, LO leakage, image rejection, harmonic/spurious analysis, EVM, and emissions performance. Develop and execute RF simulation models using tools such as Keysight ADS, AWR Microwave Office, Ansys HFSS, CST Studio, or equivalent tools for linear, nonlinear, EM, and system-level co-simulation. Select and qualify active/passive RF components and design with Ga N/Ga As/Si Ge/CMOS RFIC/MMIC devices. Define component derating, worst-case analysis, lifecycle risk, alternate part strategy, and reliability considerations for high-reliability aerospace and defence hardware. Translate system-level requirements such as frequency range, sensitivity, output power, EVM, phase noise, isolation, spur level, and dynamic range into verifiable RF circuit and subsystem specifications. Systems Architecture & Integration Contribute to RF subsystem architecture trade studies and module-level implementation planning. Lead antenna-to-baseband RF signal-chain design for radar, EW, telemetry, tactical radio, SDR, wideband receiver, and up/down-converter applications. Work with system engineers to allocate RF performance budgets and cascade gain, noise figure, linearity, filtering, isolation, and dynamic range from antenna port to ADC/DAC interface. Define LO and clock architecture, including reference clock distribution, PLL/synthesizer selection, phase noise budgeting, spur management, synchronization, and frequency settling requirements. Guide and review RF PCB layout, including stack-up selection, controlled impedance routing, RF via transitions, grounding, return-current paths, shielding, cavity isolation, connector transitions, and mixed-signal partitioning. Support mechanical and thermal integration, including RF shielding, heat sinking, enclosure effects, RF cable/connector selection, vibration considerations, and high-power PA thermal design. Support integration with FPGA, firmware, embedded software, and DSP teams from the RF hardware side, including AGC, DPD, calibration, JESD204/LVDS interfaces, timing, synchronization, and hardware control interfaces. Product Development & Qualification Define and execute RF test plans covering conducted and radiated measurements, including S-parameters, gain, gain flatness, return loss, output power, P1d B, IP3, noise figure, phase noise, EVM, ACLR/ACPR, harmonic/spurious emissions, receiver sensitivity, blocking, isolation, and EMI/EMC pre-compliance. Perform prototype bring-up, lab debugging, tuning, rework support, failure analysis, oscillation/debug, spur hunting, desense investigation, thermal drift analysis, and simulation-to-measurement correlation. Support design readiness and qualification activities for MIL-STD-461 EMC and MIL-STD-810 environmental requirements. Support production transfer, including DFM/DFT review, BOM alternate qualification, test fixture definition, production test procedures, and yield/debug support. Maintain design documentation, including schematics, RF PCB specifications, simulation reports, test procedures, test reports, analysis reports, interface control documents, compliance matrices, and verification evidence. Prepare and present PDR/CDR material, technical status, risk items, and design trade-off summaries to program managers, internal teams, and external customers. Required Qualifications Tech / M.Tech. in Electrical and Electronics Engineering, or closely related field. 8+ years of hands-on RF/microwave circuit and subsystem design experience in an aerospace, defence environment Demonstrated proficiency with at least two RF EDA tools: Keysight ADS, AWR Microwave Office, Ansys HFSS, CST Studio, or equivalent. Strong command of RF test equipment: VNA, Spectrum Analyzer, signal generator, noise-figure Analyzer, Oscilloscope and power meters. Experience designing with Ga N/Ga As/Si Ge/CMOS RFIC/MMIC devices. Familiarity with MIL-STD-461, MIL-STD-810, and MIL-HDBK-217 requirements. Strong written and verbal communication skills; ability to produce and defend technical documentation in a program environment Preferred S. or Ph.D. in RF / Microwave Engineering or related discipline Experience with Radar, Electronic warfare (EW), or Telemetry systems Familiarity with VHDL/Verilog or Python/MATLAB for test automation and signal processing support. Employee status and commitments Permanent full-time role based at our Hyderabad office with often onsite client visit. Overtime may be required to ensure client projects to be delivered on time. Develop DSP algorithms for Digital Communication systems and Radar Signal Processing . Design algorithms for: Modulation & demodulation (PCM/FM, SOQPSK, CPM, QPSK, QAM etc.) Synchronization (carrier, symbol, timing recovery) Channel coding & decoding (LDPC, Turbo, Reed-Solomon, etc.) Filtering, estimation, and detection algorithms Radar signal processing techniques Implement algorithms using MATLAB / Python for modelling and simulation. Convert algorithms into high-performance implementations in C/C++ or FPGA-friendly architectures using RTL. Validate algorithms through simulation, mathematical analysis, and test data. Analyze existing algorithm implementations and improve: Accuracy Computational efficiency Latency Robustness in real-world conditions Optimize algorithms for hardware acceleration platforms (FPGA/GPU/embedded processors). Work closely with FPGA, embedded software, and RF teams to integrate algorithms into system-level designs. Support testing, debugging, and performance evaluation of deployed systems. Systems Architecture & Integration Contribute to RF subsystem architecture trade studies and module-level implementation planning. Lead antenna-to-baseband RF signal-chain design for radar, EW, telemetry, tactical radio, SDR, wideband receiver, and up/down-converter applications. Work with system engineers to allocate RF performance budgets and cascade gain, noise figure, linearity, filtering, isolation, and dynamic range from antenna port to ADC/DAC interface. Define LO and clock architecture, including reference clock distribution, PLL/synthesizer selection, phase noise budgeting, spur management, synchronization, and frequency settling requirements. Guide and review RF PCB layout, including stack-up selection, controlled impedance routing, RF via transitions, grounding, return-current paths, shielding, cavity isolation, connector transitions, and mixed-signal partitioning. Support mechanical and thermal integration, including RF shielding, heat sinking, enclosure effects, RF cable/connector selection, vibration considerations, and high-power PA thermal design. Support integration with FPGA, firmware, embedded software, and DSP teams from the RF hardware side, including AGC, DPD, calibration, JESD204/LVDS interfaces, timing, synchronization, and hardware control interfaces. Experience: Apply Senior RF & Microwave Hardware Engineer + About Us We are a group of young and enthusiastic engineers, domain experts providing turnkey solutions to challenging requirements in Signal Processing. We work on leading technologies in Signal Processing solving problems in Defence and Aerospace fields. Our solutions range from tactical radios to radars, and from research to mission critical applications. About the role As a Senior RF Hardware Design Engineer, you will play a key role in the architecture, design, simulation, implementation, bring-up, and verification of RF and microwave hardware subsystems for aerospace and defence applications. The role includes RF signal-chain design from antenna port to baseband, including LNAs, PAs, mixers, filters, RF switches, attenuators, PLLs, frequency synthesizers, clock/LO distribution, and wideband RF front-end modules operating up to 40 GHz. The engineer will translate system-level requirements into circuit-level specifications and support the complete hardware development cycle from concept to qualification and production support. Key Responsibilities Circuit Design & Analysis Design and optimize RF/microwave circuits and subsystems, including LNAs, PAs, mixers, filters, RF switches, attenuators, VCOs, PLLs, frequency synthesizers, clock/LO distribution circuits, and RF front-end modules up to 40 GHz. Perform RF system and circuit-level analysis, including link budget, cascaded gain/noise figure, IP2/IP3, P1d B, dynamic range, SFDR, phase noise, jitter, LO leakage, image rejection, harmonic/spurious analysis, EVM, and emissions performance. Develop and execute RF simulation models using tools such as Keysight ADS, AWR Microwave Office, Ansys HFSS, CST Studio, or equivalent tools for linear, nonlinear, EM, and system-level co-simulation. Select and qualify active/passive RF components and design with Ga N/Ga As/Si Ge/CMOS RFIC/MMIC devices. Define component derating, worst-case analysis, lifecycle risk, alternate part strategy, and reliability considerations for high-reliability aerospace and defence hardware. Translate system-level requirements such as frequency range, sensitivity, output power, EVM, phase noise, isolation, spur level, and dynamic range into verifiable RF circuit and subsystem specifications. Systems Architecture & Integration Contribute to RF subsystem architecture trade studies and module-level implementation planning. Lead antenna-to-baseband RF signal-chain design for radar, EW, telemetry, tactical radio, SDR, wideband receiver, and up/down-converter applications. Work with system engineers to allocate RF performance budgets and cascade gain, noise figure, linearity, filtering, isolation, and dynamic range from antenna port to ADC/DAC interface. Define LO and clock architecture, including reference clock distribution, PLL/synthesizer selection, phase noise budgeting, spur management, synchronization, and frequency settling requirements. Guide and review RF PCB layout, including stack-up selection, controlled impedance routing, RF via transitions, grounding, return-current paths, shielding, cavity isolation, connector transitions, and mixed-signal partitioning. Support mechanical and thermal integration, including RF shielding, heat sinking, enclosure effects, RF cable/connector selection, vibration considerations, and high-power PA thermal design. Support integration with FPGA, firmware, embedded software, and DSP teams from the RF hardware side, including AGC, DPD, calibration, JESD204/LVDS interfaces, timing, synchronization, and hardware control interfaces. Product Development & Qualification Define and execute RF test plans covering conducted and radiated measurements, including S-parameters, gain, gain flatness, return loss, output power, P1d B, IP3, noise figure, phase noise, EVM, ACLR/ACPR, harmonic/spurious emissions, receiver sensitivity, blocking, isolation, and EMI/EMC pre-compliance. Perform prototype bring-up, lab debugging, tuning, rework support, failure analysis, oscillation/debug, spur hunting, desense investigation, thermal drift analysis, and simulation-to-measurement correlation. Support design readiness and qualification activities for MIL-STD-461 EMC and MIL-STD-810 environmental requirements. Support production transfer, including DFM/DFT review, BOM alternate qualification, test fixture definition, production test procedures, and yield/debug support. Maintain design documentation, including schematics, RF PCB specifications, simulation reports, test procedures, test reports, analysis reports, interface control documents, compliance matrices, and verification evidence. Prepare and present PDR/CDR material, technical status, risk items, and design trade-off summaries to program managers, internal teams, and external customers. Required Qualifications Tech / M.Tech. in Electrical and Electronics Engineering, or closely related field. 8+ years of hands-on RF/microwave circuit and subsystem design experience in an aerospace, defence environment Demonstrated proficiency with at least two RF EDA tools: Keysight ADS, AWR Microwave Office, Ansys HFSS, CST Studio, or equivalent. Strong command of RF test equipment: VNA, Spectrum Analyzer, signal generator, noise-figure Analyzer, Oscilloscope and power meters. Experience designing with Ga N/Ga As/Si Ge/CMOS RFIC/MMIC devices. Familiarity with MIL-STD-461, MIL-STD-810, and MIL-HDBK-217 requirements. Strong written and verbal communication skills; ability to produce and defend technical documentation in a program environment Preferred S. or Ph.D. in RF / Microwave Engineering or related discipline Experience with Radar, Electronic warfare (EW), or Telemetry systems Familiarity with VHDL/Verilog or Python/MATLAB for test automation and signal processing support. Employee status and commitments Permanent full-time role based at our Hyderabad office with often onsite client visit. Overtime may be required to ensure client projects to be delivered on time. Collaborative Culture: Join a collaborative and supportive work environment where your contributions are valued and recognized. Experience: Apply Sr. DSP Algorithm Engineer + About Us We are a dynamic team of engineers, researchers, and domain experts who build advanced signal processing solutions for Defence, Aerospace, and Research applications . Our work spans high-performance communication systems, Telemetry Receivers, Radar Processing, and mission-critical signal processing platforms. We focus on solving complex real-world problems by developing state-of-the-art DSP algorithms and high-performance implementations for RF, FPGA, Embedded Processors, and high-speed computing platforms. About the role We are looking for a Sr. Algorithm Developer – DSP who can design, analyze, and implement advanced signal processing algorithms from first principles. This role requires strong theoretical foundations in DSP and communications, along with the ability to translate research literature (IEEE papers, standards, and technical publications) into working algorithms and optimized implementations. The role also involves studying existing algorithms and improving their performance, robustness, and computational efficiency for real-world deployment. The candidate will work on communication and radar signal processing algorithms including modulators, demodulators, synchronization techniques, channel coding, detection, estimation, and performance optimization. Key Responsibilities Study and derive algorithms from IEEE papers, research publications, standards, and technical documentation . Develop DSP algorithms for Digital Communication systems and Radar Signal Processing . Design algorithms for: Modulation & demodulation (PCM/FM, SOQPSK, CPM, QPSK, QAM etc.) Synchronization (carrier, symbol, timing recovery) Channel coding & decoding (LDPC, Turbo, Reed-Solomon, etc.) Filtering, estimation, and detection algorithms Radar signal processing techniques Implement algorithms using MATLAB / Python for modelling and simulation. Convert algorithms into high-performance implementations in C/C++ or FPGA-friendly architectures using RTL. Validate algorithms through simulation, mathematical analysis, and test data. Analyze existing algorithm implementations and improve: Accuracy Computational efficiency Latency Robustness in real-world conditions Optimize algorithms for hardware acceleration platforms (FPGA/GPU/embedded processors). Work closely with FPGA, embedded software, and RF teams to integrate algorithms into system-level designs. Support testing, debugging, and performance evaluation of deployed systems. Participate in technical problem solving and architectural discussions. Document algorithms, simulation results, and performance evaluations. Stay updated with latest developments in signal processing and communication theory. Required Qualifications Bachelor’s or Master's degree in Electronics & Communication Engineering from a reputed institution. 4–8 years of experience in system development involving both software and hardware components. Strong understanding of DSP, RF systems, and communications/radar technologies. Proficiency in one or more tools/languages: Lab VIEW, C/C++, MATLAB, Verilog/VHDL. Experience managing small technical teams and working in cross-functional setups. Familiarity with projects involving government agencies or DRDO is a plus. Excellent communication and documentation skills for client and internal reporting. Strong fundamentals in: Digital Signal Processing Digital Communications Probability & Random Processes Estimation Theory Employee status and commitments Permanent full-time position, located at our Hyderabad office, with regular on-site visits to clients and vendor locations. Develop and execute RF simulation models using tools such as Keysight ADS, AWR Microwave Office, Ansys HFSS, CST Studio, or equivalent tools for linear, nonlinear, EM, and system-level co-simulation. Systems Architecture & Integration Contribute to RF subsystem architecture trade studies and module-level implementation planning.
